judged_text: destroy calls `host.destroy` on the result of `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil check, raising NoMethodError when the id no longer exists. Two admins deleting the same host makes the second DELETE return a 500 instead of a 404, and because the component's `destroyRecord().then()` has no rejection handler the row silently stays in the admin list looking undeleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`. If the record is already deleted (e.g., two admins delete same host), `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a not-found response. On the client side, the component’s `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch(...)`, so a failed DELETE won’t remove the row and (absent any global handler) won’t be handled locally.
